append_only.scope: Append a cautious identity match and an initial XRP/crypto-focused inventory from one matching public YouTube channel. This is not an exhaustive export of the channel's approximately 1.3K videos.

basis: On the iHeart episode page titled 'Crypto Panics! with Dr. Kamilah Stevenson' (June 11, 2026), the guest's auto-generated transcript at 40:07 says she is on YouTube at 'doctor Camilla Stevenson'; the same first-person answer gives the X display phrase 'cam i am cam Stevenson' and Instagram display name 'Kamilla Stevenson'.
The same transcript explicitly warns that fake pages exist. The transcript is auto-generated and the publisher says accuracy is not guaranteed.
The YouTube handle URL resolves to a channel displayed as 'Kamilah Stevenson'.

Vling's channel analytics page maps channel ID UCqUPJMQdkCN6lsLVDnichPA to the same Kamilah Stevenson name and matching first-person channel description. It reported 143K subscribers, approximately 1.3K videos, United States, and join date 2015-08-25 at its recent crawl.

Direct YouTube search results for the listed video IDs attribute the creator to 'Kamilah Stevenson' with channel-size snapshots around 138K–140K followers; Glasp transcripts for several of the same videos begin with the speaker identifying herself as 'Camila Stevenson'.
limitations: This is a high-confidence match between a public channel and a podcast guest, not legal identity verification.
No direct authenticated cross-link from the creator's X or Instagram profile to the YouTube channel was captured.
The iHeart transcript is machine-generated and may mis-transcribe names.
Third-party analytics and view/like counts are snapshots, not authoritative YouTube API exports.
The creator states that fake pages exist; similarly named channels are excluded unless their channel ID matches.
